10546.correction: In a unison texture, both the pitch and rhythm of the part must be the same. In a homophonic texture, only the rhythm needs to be the same - the parts can play different notes or chords. Parts played in octaves are also classed as a unison texture.

558.belief: If the bass stays on the same note, this is a pedal.
558.statement: If the bass stays on the same note, this is a pedal.
558.correction: This is not quite true. It is only a pedal if the bass note stays the same while the chords change above it. If the chords do not change, it cannot be a pedal.

9411.belief: A solo should just use as many fast notes as possible.
9411.statement: A solo should just use as many fast notes as possible.
9411.correction: To be really effective, a solo should gradually build up in intensity. If it is extremely virtuosic from the beginning, it loses its impact. Building up to a very flashy, virtuosic climax is most effective.

10633.belief: You should use root position chords sparingly because they sound uninteresting.
10633.statement: You should use root position chords sparingly because they sound uninteresting.
10633.correction: Not necessarily. Root position chords are important because they anchor the music in the key. Most chords in a chord sequence should be root position, with some inversions used to add interst and variety.

44.belief: Only 3rds, 5ths and octaves work as disjunct intervals in a melody.
44.statement: Only 3rds, 5ths and octaves work as disjunct intervals in a melody.
44.correction: This is not true: all intervals (except sevenths) can work effectively, as long as they jump between chord tones. If intervals jump to or from non-chord tones, the melody will sound ineffective.

9035.belief: There are no 'rules' for writing a chord sequence.
9035.statement: There are no 'rules' for writing a chord sequence.
9035.correction: While to some extent this is true, in Western classical music there are very typical patterns that are used very regularly. These include the position of perfect and imperfect cadences, and what the chords do throughout the 16 bars.

4258.belief: As long as the chord tones in the chord are played, it doesn't matter how these notes are split between the 2nd violin and viola.
4258.statement: As long as the chord tones in the chord are played, it doesn't matter how these notes are split between the 2nd violin and viola.
4258.correction: This does matter. The voicing of the chord makes a big difference to how it sounds. Avoiding large intervals between those instruments, and making sure that the chords aren't very low or high pitched makes them sound effective.

2064.belief: A countermelody is just a type of accompaniment.
2064.statement: A countermelody is just a type of accompaniment.
2064.correction: It is actually quite different from an accompaniment, because it should be equally as prominent as the main melody, whereas an accompaniment is not. An accompaniment is usually also based on repeating patterns, whereas a melody does not have to be.

20.belief: The 2:3 clave starts on the same beat as the 3:2 clave.
20.statement: The 2:3 clave starts on the same beat as the 3:2 clave.
20.correction: The 2:3 clave starts with a crotchet rest. Make sure when performing or recording this that you count 'rest, 1, 2' for the '2' section of the rhythm.

4044.belief: Latin dance music all sounds the same.
4044.statement: Latin dance music all sounds the same.
4044.correction: Many of the styles of music from this region include similar features, such as syncopated rhythms, Latin percussion, Spanish lyrics etc. However, they all have distinct differences that allow us to tell the different traditions apart.

812.belief: Calypso, mento and soca are different versions of the same musical style.
812.statement: Calypso, mento and soca are different versions of the same musical style.
812.correction: Although they have superficial similarities, these are all distinct styles with different features and histories. Soca is strongly linked to calypso and can be seen as an offshoot of that style, but mento is a completely separate tradition.

6218.statement: Pupils may confuse the bossa nova clave and rumba clave with each other.
6218.correction: Break the bossa nova clave into its group of 3 and group of 2. Practise the '3' on its own, identically to the son clave. Then practise the '2' with the second note delayed by a quaver. Only once the two parts are separately learnt then combine them.

2518.belief: Drum beats should emphasise the start of each bar.
2518.statement: Drum beats should emphasise the start of each bar.
2518.correction: Most pop and rock drum beats do this, but many other musical styles do not emphasise beat one. The one-drop beat starts with a rest on beat one, and emphasises beat two and four.

4778.belief: Music from the Romantic period is all about love and romance.
4778.statement: Music from the Romantic period is all about love and romance.
4778.correction: The word Romantic in the musical sense has nothing to do with love or romance, this was just the name given to the period. The music was often intense, emotive and dramatic, and might sometimes link to ideas of love, but it was very varied.

5229.belief: The orchestra has only grown through the adding of more of the same instruments.
5229.statement: The orchestra has only grown through the adding of more of the same instruments.
5229.correction: The number of players has increased, but the variety of instruments has also increased. Many different instruments have been added to the orchestra since the 1600s, including brass, woodwind, percussion and keyboard instruments.

4768.belief: Most music in the Baroque, Classical and Romantic periods was written for an orchestra.
4768.statement: Most music in the Baroque, Classical and Romantic periods was written for an orchestra.
4768.correction: Although a lot of the most famous music now is orchestral, it was much more diverse than this - composers wrote for many different ensembles, large and small. These included solo compositions, duets, trios, quartets, quintets and many others.

5228.belief: Oratorios and anthems are essentially the same - they are both religious, with similar musical features.
5228.statement: Oratorios and anthems are essentially the same - they are both religious, with similar musical features.
5228.correction: Anthems often are a capella, whereas oratorios always have orchestral accompaniment. Oratorios are long pieces of music, consisting of numerous songs that tell a biblical story. Anthems are shorter songs that are used as part of a Christian service.

3456.belief: Harmony and tonality are the same thing.
3456.statement: Harmony and tonality are the same thing.
3456.correction: Tonality is to the type of notes and chords that are used (e.g. major). Harmony is the way the notes and chords are used within that key. Think of tonality as a language (e.g. English) and harmony as the word choice and order in a sentence.

1649.belief: Chord inversions are inserted randomly by composers.
1649.statement: Chord inversions are inserted randomly by composers.
1649.correction: Chord inversions are used to add interest by bringing subtle amounts of tension to a chord and to create smoother transitions from one chord to another. They are not chosen randomly and are used sparingly to create a particular effect.

942.belief: Changing the voicing of a chord is the same as changing the chord inversion.
942.statement: Changing the voicing of a chord is the same as changing the chord inversion.
942.correction: They are not the same thing. The inversion of the chord is determined by which note is at the bottom (the root or a different note). The voicing is how the notes are spread above this - whether they are close together or far apart.

11166.belief: Writing a vocal melody is the same as writing an instrumental melody.
11166.statement: Writing a vocal melody is the same as writing an instrumental melody.
11166.correction: Many of the same principles apply, such as phrase structure and using notes from the chords and the key. However, a vocal melody has to fit the natural rhythms and mood of the words well - we don't have to consider this with instrumental melodies.

4352.belief: The main difference between the verse and chorus is the lyrics.
4352.statement: The main difference between the verse and chorus is the lyrics.
4352.correction: Although that is an important difference, the verse and chorus usually have contrasting moods. This is achieved by creating contrasting chord sequences, textures, rhythms and melodies, not just using different lyrics.

2096.belief: To create a good countermelody, you just need two melodies playing at the same time.
2096.statement: To create a good countermelody, you just need two melodies playing at the same time.
2096.correction: It's a bit more complicated than that. An effective countermelody has to contrast with the main melody, so that it can be heard. This is done by choosing an appropriate timbre and octave, and using the 'space' in the main melody.

186.belief: Afrobeat and Afrobeats are the same thing.
186.statement: Afrobeat and Afrobeats are the same thing.
186.correction: Afrobeat is a specific genre from the 1960s/1970s based on a fusion of West African music with funk and soul. Afrobeats is a broad term for many modern genres that are different fusions from across the continent, but have a few common features.

9463.belief: South Asian (or Indian) music is a genre itself.
9463.statement: South Asian (or Indian) music is a genre itself.
9463.correction: South Asian music is as diverse as European music. There are many different styles linked to different groups of people, places and traditions. What we are looking at here are a few ways that South Asian genres have been fused with Western genres.

5922.belief: The Punjab is part of India.
5922.statement: The Punjab is part of India.
5922.correction: The Punjab is an area split between modern-day India and Pakistan. It has a distinct history, culture and traditions as a region, one of which is bhangra.

649.belief: Bhangra is a style of music from South Asia.
649.statement: Bhangra is a style of music from South Asia.
649.correction: Bhangra in its modern form is an example of musical fusion, between Punjabi traditional bhangra and Western popular styles of music.

650.belief: Bhangra is a traditional style of music that doesn't use music technology extensively.
650.statement: Bhangra is a traditional style of music that doesn't use music technology extensively.
650.correction: Modern bhangra uses many of the tools that are available to musicians now, including different applications of music technology. It uses these to enhance the music, while still having its roots embedded in the traditional features of Punjabi bhangra.

10862.belief: Video games composers just have to compose different music for different scenes, like a film composer.
10862.statement: Video games composers just have to compose different music for different scenes, like a film composer.
10862.correction: To be really effective, it is more complex than this. The music they compose must be able to repeat indefinitely, while sounding musically interesting. It also has to seamlessly transition into different moods, reacting to changes in the action.

1869.belief: Complex music sounds most exciting and energetic.
1869.statement: Complex music sounds most exciting and energetic.
1869.correction: Not necessarily - sometimes the most energetic music is that which emphasises the pulse and uses driving rhythms. Sometimes if music is too complex, with many busy layers of sound, it can sound chaotic and messy rather than energetic.

8849.belief: Reharmonising a melody is as simple as playing it a third higher.
8849.statement: Reharmonising a melody is as simple as playing it a third higher.
8849.correction: While this can be effective, for certain melodies this won't work effectively. Instead, experimenting with the harmonised melody both above and below the main melody is key, as well as experimenting with 3rds and 6ths.

3528.belief: In horizontal resequencing, new musical sections should completely contrast with the preceeding section.
3528.statement: In horizontal resequencing, new musical sections should completely contrast with the preceeding section.
3528.correction: There should be contrast, but there also needs to be a feeling of continuity. Using some consistent features (like tempo, key, timbre) can help to create a feeling of some continuity, while still creating a large contrast.

10040.belief: Sudden tempo changes do not work in horizontal resequencing.
10040.statement: Sudden tempo changes do not work in horizontal resequencing.
10040.correction: Sometimes tempo changes can sound jarring and unnatural, but sometimes video game composers want to create a sudden change of pace. If done carefully, tempo changes can work effectively.

551.belief: All Baroque music is contrapuntal / polyphonic.
551.statement: All Baroque music is contrapuntal / polyphonic.
551.correction: Textures are varied in the Baroque period, but use of contrapuntal/polyphonic textures was very common and contrasts with the later Classical period. This is a typical texture of the period, but not the only one.

9427.belief: Sonata form and a sonata are the same thing.
9427.statement: Sonata form and a sonata are the same thing.
9427.correction: This is a common misconception. Sonata form is a structure in a piece that has a exposition, development and recapitulation. A sonata is a three-movement composition for solo instrument. The first movement of a sonata is normally in sonata form.

9001.belief: Romantic music is related to love and romance.
9001.statement: Romantic music is related to love and romance.
9001.correction: This is not the case - the name is not related to that. Romantic composers focused on creating expression, emotion and evocative moods in their music. Sometimes this would have links with love, but not always.

5469.belief: Each period had a single defining texture (e.g. Baroque = polyphonic).
5469.statement: Each period had a single defining texture (e.g. Baroque = polyphonic).
5469.correction: There were typical uses of texture for each period. For example, Baroque composers often used polyphonic textures, much more than Classical composers. However, within each period, there were examples of all textures being used and lots of variety.

4961.belief: Non-functional harmony sounds the same as functional harmony.
4961.statement: Non-functional harmony sounds the same as functional harmony.
4961.correction: While some of the chords might be the same, the difference is in the role. In functional harmony, chords have specific roles (e.g. V coming before I to create resolution). In non-functional harmony, any chord can be used whenever the composer wants.

10696.belief: Using disjunct intervals in a melody means the notes can be placed anywhere.
10696.statement: Using disjunct intervals in a melody means the notes can be placed anywhere.
10696.correction: Disjunct intervals need a sense of order to the music and should be used in some sort of pattern in the same way that conjunct intervals should.

3455.belief: Harmony and chords are the same thing.
3455.statement: Harmony and chords are the same thing.
3455.correction: Although the harmony is created by the different notes of the chord progression, harmony also includes all parts in the music including the melodic line.

1876.belief: To compose a rhythm we need to consider notation first.
1876.statement: To compose a rhythm we need to consider notation first.
1876.correction: It is important to encourage pupils not to be restricted by only rhythms they can notate and for them to experiment with rhythmic patterns that they like musically. Highlight that individual note durations such as a crotchet are not rhythms.

5517.belief: A piece of music has a fixed texture all the way through.
5517.statement: A piece of music has a fixed texture all the way through
5517.correction: Although we can describe some pieces of music as particular textures overall there are often sections within pieces where the texture changes.

3812.belief: An instrument only has one timbre.
3812.statement: An instrument only has one timbre.
3812.correction: An instrument can have a few different timbres. Give examples of how instruments can change the sound they make.

9211.belief: Sequence, retrograde and inversion are they only way to develop ideas and they have to be used perfectly.
9211.statement: Sequence, retrograde and inversion are they only way to develop ideas and they have to be used perfectly.
9211.correction: Sequences, retrograde and inversion provide a concrete way for pupils to show development in their melodic ideas, but providing there is some similarity or recognisable quality in repeated ideas, any subtle changes within melodic ideas can work.

5378.belief: A pedal note is just a long, low note.
5378.statement: A pedal note is just a long, low note.
5378.correction: A pedal note is a consistent pitch usually in the bass whilst the chords change. Encourage pupils to listen to and experiment with the pitch they choose for a pedal to hear the effect it has on the harmony.

507.belief: Augmentation and diminution are not the same as augmented and diminished.
507.statement: Augmentation and diminution are not the same as augmented and diminished.
507.correction: Augmentation and diminution are devices that affect the rhythm of music. Augmented and diminished are types of chords and refer to the harmony of music.

760.belief: Broken chords have to be in the triad position where the root is the lowest note.
760.statement: Broken chords have to be in the triad position where the root is the lowest note.
760.correction: Broken chords like block chords can be played in different inversions and this can make them more interesting.

2028.belief: Contrasting sections should be totally different to other sections in a composition.
2028.statement: Contrasting sections should be totally different to other sections in a composition.
2028.correction: Contrasting sections of music can be derived from some of the same ideas but should have their own recognisable melodic and harmonic ideas.

8743.belief: A raga is just a scale.
8743.statement: A raga is just a scale.
8743.correction: A raga is a bit more complex than being just a scale. It has specific times of day, moods and emotions associated with it, as well as rules about how it should be played.

10163.correction: Teental sounds to us like it could be in 4/4, but this is just a coincidence. North Indian classical musicians don't think of time signature in the same way that we do - the tala is what structures the time and they can be many different lengths.

208.belief: The alap - gat - jhala structure is just about changes in tempo from slow, to medium to fast.
208.statement: The alap - gat - jhala structure is just about changes in tempo from slow, to medium to fast.
208.correction: While the tempo does change, the bigger changes are around melody. The alap explores the raga freely, the gat is more structured and the jhala is heavily improvised and virtuosic.

2123.belief: A cross rhythm is when two players play in different time signatures.
2123.statement: A cross rhythm is when two players play in different time signatures.
2123.correction: A cross rhythm only sounds like there are different time signatures at the same time, but in reality they both use the same time signature (but sound otherwise).

2160.correction: While the majority of modern Western dance music is in 4/4, dance music around the world (and throughout history) often uses different time signatures, including 3/.4, 6/8 and 12/8, as well as others.

4547.belief: Melody and accompaniment is not a homophonic texture.
4547.statement: Melody and accompaniment is not a homophonic texture.
4547.correction: There are different kinds of homophonic texture. A chordal homophonic texture is one in which all parts play the same rhythm. Melody and accompaniment is also called melody-dominated homophony, where there is a homophonic texture with a melody above.

1911.belief: A concerto grosso is exactly the same as a concerto, just with more than one soloist.
1911.statement: A concerto grosso is exactly the same as a concerto, just with more than one soloist.
1911.correction: Because there is more than one soloist, composers can play around with texture and interaction more in a concerto grosso. This means that often there is more variety of interaction between parts in a concerto grosso than a solo concerto.

792.correction: Many cadenzas are composed, but it is common for soloists to improvise (or slightly change) cadenzas to make them more unique and to further show off their own skill.

9002.belief: Romantic music is romantic (i.e. about love).
9002.statement: Romantic music is romantic (i.e. about love).
9002.correction: Romantic music is generally expressive and emotional, but is not necessarily linked to the emotion of love. The emotions can be anything from dramatic and terrifying to dark and mournful. The name comes from a broader artistic movement.

5509.belief: Piano concertos are just the same as other concertos.
5509.statement: Piano concertos are just the same as other concertos.
5509.correction: Not quite. Because of the unique abilities of the piano - including its range and ability to play multiple lines at once - composers use it slightly differently to other instruments. This includes using it to accompany itself, or the orchestra.

3440.belief: Hand drum technique is the same across the world.
3440.statement: Hand drum technique is the same across the world.
3440.correction: Techniques are very different on different hand drums around the world. Tabla, doumbek and djembe all use very different techniques, for example, the doumbek technique uses fingertips in a way that djembe does not.

12.correction: There is an infinite possible number of notes. Imagine that an octave is a cake. We can divide it into 12 equal slices (12 Western notes) or 24 smaller slices (the Arabic system). In theory, we could divide it into any number of slices/notes.

3880.belief: Israeli music is very similar to other Middle Eastern music because Israel is in the Middle East.
3880.statement: Israeli music is very similar to other Middle Eastern music because Israel is in the Middle East.
3880.correction: Israeli folk music has a very different history to other music from the region, as it was influenced by Jewish migrants from other parts of the world. Jewish folk music uses many European instruments and has similarities with European folk music.

4769.belief: Music for dance must have a regular pulse (in 2, 3 or 4).
4769.statement: Music for dance must have a regular pulse (in 2, 3 or 4).
4769.correction: While most Western dance music has a regular time signature, in other parts of the world it is common to dance to music with irregular time signatures, such as 5/8 and 7/8.

713.belief: The bouzouki sounds the same as a guitar.
713.statement: The bouzouki sounds the same as a guitar.
713.correction: The bouzouki has very specific techniques that give it its characteristic sound. These include use of tremolo, slides and thirds. Although these can be used on the guitar, they are not as common as on the bouzouki.

4983.belief: If the notes of a melody are changed, that just makes it a new melody.
4983.statement: If the notes of a melody are changed, that just makes it a new melody.
4983.correction: Changing the notes of a melody does create a new melody, but if it is still recognisable as related to the original, we can consider it a developed version of the melody. If it is unrecognisable, then it is not a development but a totally new melody.

3626.belief: Imitation and a countermelody are the same thing.
3626.statement: Imitation and a countermelody are the same thing.
3626.correction: They are related, but not the same. Imitation has to include copying part of the melody, normally immediately. A countermelody usually tries to contrast with the main melody so that it can be heard clearly separately.

4772.belief: If music has a key, it must be diatonic.
4772.statement: If music has a key, it must be diatonic.
4772.correction: Not necessarily. A piece of music can have a key, but use notes from outside of it. This would be chromatic. It could also have a key, but use some microtones as well, meaning it is microtonal.

1650.belief: Chord IV and V sound the same, so plagal and perfect cadences sound the same.
1650.statement: Chord IV and V sound the same, so plagal and perfect cadences sound the same.
1650.correction: They sound similar, but not identical. Picking out the bass note is the key - if you can hear that note, you can work out how it relates to the tonic, so can work out which chord (and cadence) you are listening to.

4707.belief: A modulation is when the chords don't use the tonic.
4707.statement: A modulation is when the chords don't use the tonic.
4707.correction: A modulation is actually when the tonic changes. Sometimes music can sound like it will modulate, but then it stays in the same key. For a true modulation, it must feel like the tonic itself has changed.

3813.belief: Instrumental timbres in families can be identified with pitch.
3813.statement: Instrumental timbres in families can be identified with pitch.
3813.correction: This isn't always the case. Instruments such as the trombone and French horn have a similiar pitch and the oboe and cor anglais pitch ranges cross over, so it's important that pupils think about the timbres to identify instruments correctly.

3662.belief: It is impossible to memorise the timbre of all of the different instruments around the world.
3662.statement: It is impossible to memorise the timbre of all of the different instruments around the world.
3662.correction: Yes, it would be impossible. However, learning to identify some of the key instruments is valuable - these are often heard in styles across different cultures, so learning the sound of the most common is important as a well-rounded musician.

2957.belief: Female voices are always higher pitched than male voices.
2957.statement: Female voices are always higher pitched than male voices.
2957.correction: While this is mostly true, alto and tenor ranges overlap. A low alto voice can be as low as a tenor. Alongside this, men can use the falsetto technique to sing much higher than their normal range, in some cases higher than female voices.

4782.belief: Music technology consists solely of DAWs and computer-based technology.
4782.statement: Music technology consists solely of DAWs and computer-based technology.
4782.correction: For modern musicians, computer-based tools such as DAWs are a brilliant way of using technology. However, music technology is much broader than this - synthesisers, amplification, turntables and drum machines are just a few examples.

3524.belief: Homophonic and melody and accompaniment textures are the same thing.
3524.statement: Homophonic and melody and accompaniment textures are the same thing.
3524.correction: Melody and accompaniment is a specific type of homophonic texture, often called melody-dominated homophony. This is different to a chordal homophonic texture. To avoid confusion, it is easiest to treat melody and accompaniment as a separate texture.

1886.belief: Compound time signatures create more complex sounding music and aren't used often.
1886.statement: Compound time signatures create more complex sounding music and aren't used often.
1886.correction: This isn't strictly true. Compound time signatures are extremely common, including in popular music styles. While the theory of them is slightly more complex than simple time signatures, to compose or play using them is not particularly difficult.

10174.belief: Tempo markings are a precise indication of speed.
10174.statement: Tempo markings are a precise indication of speed.
10174.correction: Most tempo markings (like allegro) are a rough indication of the speed, but not an exact measurement. Composers usually leave it up to the performers to determine the exact speed. Often in modern music they will indicate a specific speed using BPM.

5691.belief: Polyrhythm and cross rhythm are the same thing.
5691.statement: Polyrhythm and cross rhythm are the same thing.
5691.correction: They are related, but not the same. A polyrhythm doesn't necessarily have to create different senses of pulse - it can just have different rhythms playing together. A cross rhythm has to create different senses of pulse at the same time.

3601.belief: Idiomatic rhythms are rhythms that are only used in a specific style.
3601.statement: Idiomatic rhythms are rhythms that are only used in a specific style.
3601.correction: Idiomatic rhythms are rhythms that are typically associated with that style, but can also be heard in different styles. For example, while the skank rhythm is very idiomatic in reggae, there are many other styles that also repeat off-beat quavers.

5165.belief: There is only one type of accent.
5165.statement: There is only one type of accent.
5165.correction: The regular accent is the most common, but composers often indicate more specific articulation by using other accents such as marcato and sforzando. These can be difficult to distinguish by ear, but as a performer you should be familiar with them.

4282.belief: Longer note values (like minims) are impossible to verbalise, because the words sound the same as a crotchet.
4282.statement: Longer note values (like minims) are impossible to verbalise, because the words sound the same as a crotchet.
4282.correction: Longer note values are tricky to verbalise. A minim uses one syllable, just like a crotchet. The key is to make sure you count how many beats they last for - that will help you tell the difference between crotchets, minims and longer notes.

10638.belief: You can use the same verbalisation in compound time as simple time signatures.
10638.statement: You can use the same verbalisation in compound time as simple time signatures.
10638.correction: This will create problems, because there are 3 quavers in each beat in compound time. The counting method in compound time avoids confusion by ensuring there are three quavers in each beat.

167.belief: Only advanced musicians can work out a set of notes by listening to them.
167.statement: Only advanced musicians can work out a set of notes by listening to them.
167.correction: Anyone can work out notes by ear, if they practise the correct strategies. Identifying the melodic shape, representing it with a line, then carefully converting it into notes is an effective first step in melodic dictation.

9333.belief: Singing is only useful for singers.
9333.statement: Singing is only useful for singers.
9333.correction: When identifying intervals, singing is incredibly useful, even for those who aren't confident singers. Hearing the intervals back through singing or humming allows us to compare them to the reference melodies. Without this, it is much harder.

11120.belief: Working out the notes of a whole melody by ear is a very difficult musical skill.
11120.statement: Working out the notes of a whole melody by ear is a very difficult musical skill.
11120.correction: While it seems challenging, if you break it down into small steps - individual intervals - it is no more difficult than working out one interval. Take it one step at a time in small chunks and it is completely achievable.

2269.belief: A description of timbre should only describe the sound qualities heard.
2269.statement: A description of timbre should only describe the sound qualities heard.
2269.correction: While this should be included, it is also important to remember to describe the instruments that have been used, and if they from a particular ensemble. Remember that one instrument can also create multiple timbres.

4356.belief: The main thing I need to remember for long-form answers is the elements acronym (e.g. MAD T SHIRTT).
4356.statement: The main thing I need to remember for long-form answers is the elements acronym (e.g. MAD T SHIRTT).
4356.correction: These acronyms do help us to remember what the elements are, but it is much more important in these longer descriptions to ensure answers are clearly structured, thorough and concise, and that correct technical vocabulary is used for each element.

2262.belief: When describing music, just describing each element is enough.
2262.statement: When describing music, just describing each element is enough.
2262.correction: For some questions, it may be appropriate just to describe each element. However, often we should give a more sophisticated response that links each element to the compositional purpose - why did the composer use that and why is it suitable?
